stories.title: Clarion Partners Closes $206M Vegas Industrial Buy
stories.excerpt: Clarion Partners has acquired Golden Triangle Logistics Center, a 1.3-million-square-foot, Class A industrial portfolio in North Las Vegas, Nevada, in a deal worth $205.6 million, according to published reports. Golden Triangle Logistics Center consists of three distribution facilities located at 2655, 2815 and 3375 E. Washburn Road in North Las Vegas. Spanning approximately 64.5 acres, the portfolio offers access to Interstate 15 and the Clark County 215 Beltway, positioning tenants to efficiently serve major Western U.S. population centers. The campus, 84% leased at time of sale, features 36- to 37-foot clear heights, ESFR sprinkler systems, expansive truck courts, 189 dock-high loading positions and a sizeable, secured trailer storage yard. Newmark Executive Managing Director Andrew Briner and Vice Chairman Ken White represented the seller, Washington Capital. Newmark Co-Head, U.S. Capital Markets Kevin Shannon provided executive oversight in the deal. According to Newmark, the transaction marks the largest industrial sale completed in the Vegas metro since 2023. bullets: Clarion Partners acquires 1.3M SF industrial portfolio, North Las Vegas, $206M.
Golden Triangle Logistics 84% leased, I-15/215 Beltway access, 36-37 ft clear heights.
Largest Vegas industrial sale since 2023; signals continued logistics demand West.
stories.summary: Clarion Partners closed a $205.6M acquisition of Golden Triangle Logistics Center, a three-building, 1.3M SF Class A industrial portfolio on 64.5 acres in North Las Vegas. The asset was 84% leased at sale and features institutional specifications (36–37 ft clear heights, ESFR sprinkler systems, 189 dock-high positions) positioned for regional distribution serving Western U.S. markets via I-15 and the 215 Beltway. This marks the largest Vegas metro industrial sale since 2023.
stories.impact: Las Vegas industrial market remains a focal point for logistics capital amid consistent Western distribution demand. The 84% occupancy and institutional buyer confidence signal durable rental demand in Las Vegas submarket; developers should monitor absorption rates and land availability in I-15 and 215 corridors for future logistics/light industrial development opportunities.

stories.title: CP Group-Led JV Lands $272M for Mixed-Use Boca Raton Campus
stories.excerpt: A joint venture led by CP Group has secured $271.5 million in financing from a Blackstone affiliate for the acquisition and planned renovation of the 30-Acre Mizner Park complex in Downtown Boca Raton, Fla., property records show. The JV paid $193 million for the 838,840-square-foot Mizner Park, which sits adjacent to the Boca Raton Museum of Art, along North Dixie Highway, near the Brightline station. The property houses 268,391 square feet of office space, 276,461 square feet of retail space and 272 apartments across 293,988 square feet. CP Group originally developed Mizner Park between 1991 and 1999 on land owned by the city. Last week, the Boca Raton-based investor gained control of the asset — with partners Georgetown Company, Acre and StepStone — through ground leases. The transaction breaks down to $113.1 million for the retail component, $46.3 million for the residential component, and $33.5 million for the office component, according to documents filed to Palm Beach County. The previous lessee, Brookfield, gained control of Mizner Park in 2018 through its $9 billion acquisition of General Growth Properties. “Our goal is to bring new energy and investment to this landmark destination while preserving what has made it such an important part of the community and a jewel of the city for generations,” Angelo Bianco, managing partner of CP Group, said in a statement. The surplus in financing from Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies will likely fund the planned renovations, which include upgrades to the building’s facades, landscaping, back-of-house infrastructure, and office common areas. Acre will oversee the multifamily component of Mizner Park, including a renovation. JLL’s Danny Finkle, Matt McCormack and Michael Roukis represented the sellers, while Danny Kaufman, Preston Bacon and Paul Stasaitis, also from JLL, arranged financing. bullets: CP Group JV secures $271.5M Blackstone financing, Mizner Park, Boca Raton acquisition.
30-acre mixed-use campus: 272 apts, 268K SF office, 276K SF retail; Brightline adjacent.
Residential valued at $46.3M; repositioning signals downtown density play near transit.
stories.summary: A joint venture led by CP Group (with Georgetown Company, Acre, and StepStone) secured $271.5M in financing from a Blackstone affiliate to acquire and renovate the 30-acre Mizner Park in Downtown Boca Raton. The 838,840 SF mixed-use asset comprises 272 apartments, 268K SF office, and 276K SF retail, positioned adjacent to the Boca Raton Museum of Art and near the Brightline station. The purchase price was $193M, with the residential component valued at $46.3M.
stories.impact: Brightline proximity in South Florida is a development accelerant; CP Group's repositioning of Mizner Park signals institutional confidence in downtown Boca Raton density and transit-oriented mixed-use. The $46.3M residential value within a $193M acquisition reflects compressed unit economics; developers should monitor Brightline ridership, residential demand in downtown Boca Raton corridors, and competitive delivery timelines for similar transit-proximate infill projects.

stories.title: Panattoni Obtains $59M Refi Loan on Arizona Industrial Property
stories.excerpt: Panattoni Development Company has secured a $58.72 million refinance loan on Northern Parkway Logistics Center, a 445,187 square foot, Class A industrial portfolio located at 12815 W. Northern Ave. and 12795 W. Northern Ave. in Glendale, Arizona. The financing was arranged by JLL Capital Markets. Completed in 2025, Northern Parkway Logistics Center consists of three industrial buildings situated on approximately 30 acres within Northern Parkway Logistics Hub, a master-planned industrial development in Phoenix’s West Valley. The project was 57.9%-leased at closing and features institutional-quality specifications designed to accommodate a range of logistics, distribution, manufacturing and industrial users. Northern Parkway Logistics Center is strategically positioned between Loop 101 and Loop 303 with direct access to the region’s primary transportation corridors, providing efficient connectivity throughout Metro Phoenix and to major Western U.S. markets. JLL Senior Director Jason Carlos, along with Associate Frank Choumas, Analyst Ross Jorgensen and Analyst Andrew Mings, arranged the three-year, floating-rate loan through Mesa West Capital. bullets: Panattoni refinances Northern Parkway Logistics Center, Phoenix West Valley, $58.72M.
445K SF, three buildings, 57.9% leased at close; 2025 delivery.
Floating-rate refi signals builder confidence; West Valley industrial supply pressure emerging.
stories.summary: Panattoni Development secured a $58.72M three-year floating-rate refinance on Northern Parkway Logistics Center, a newly completed 445,187 SF three-building portfolio in Glendale, Arizona (West Valley). The asset was 57.9% leased at closing and features institutional logistics specifications positioned between Loop 101 and Loop 303. The loan was arranged by JLL and funded through Mesa West Capital.
stories.impact: Northern Parkway's below-60% lease rate at 2025 close, despite institutional specs and prime loop connectivity, suggests West Valley industrial supply is outpacing near-term demand absorption. Developers should scrutinize West Valley deliveries and pre-leasing windows; floating-rate refinancing on a partially leased 2025 delivery implies builder/sponsor confidence in lease-up trajectory, but cap rate compression and lease spread risk are material for new starts in this submarket.

stories.title: RevKo Developing Crane-Served Houston Manufacturing Campus
stories.excerpt: RevKo Commercial Real Estate is developing AeroPoint 1960, a 457,000-square-foot manufacturing and crane-served campus in North Houston near George Bush Intercontinental Airport. The two-phase development will bring modern manufacturing space to the market. JLL’s Geoff Perrott and David Holland, along with RevKo’s Boomer White, are marketing the development. Jon Sellers, the CEO of RevKo’s development team, will lead the development. Phase I will include five (5) freestanding/manufacturing buildings totaling approximately 202,000 square feet, with delivery slated for Q3 2027. The buildings will be designed to support users requiring crane-served manufacturing space, with dedicated industrial outside storage (IOS) yards planned for each building. Phase II will add approximately 255,000 square feet of additional manufacturing space and is proposed for build-to-suit and design-build opportunities, providing flexibility for companies seeking customized facilities to support their operations. AeroPoint 1960 is positioned to address continued demand for freestanding/manufacturing and industrial outdoor storage (IOS) facilities across the Houston market. The post RevKo Developing Crane-Served Houston Manufacturing Campus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: RevKo developing AeroPoint 1960, North Houston near IAH, 457K SF crane-served campus.
Phase I: 202K SF, five buildings, Q3 2027 delivery; Phase II: 255K SF build-to-suit.
Crane-served/IOS yards address niche manufacturing demand; IAH adjacency supports aerospace/industrial tenants.
stories.summary: RevKo Commercial Real Estate is developing AeroPoint 1960, a 457K SF two-phase manufacturing and crane-served campus in North Houston near George Bush Intercontinental Airport. Phase I will deliver five freestanding manufacturing buildings (202K SF) in Q3 2027 with dedicated industrial outside storage (IOS) yards; Phase II proposes 255K SF of build-to-suit and design-build manufacturing space. The development targets users requiring crane-served manufacturing facilities.
stories.impact: IAH-proximate manufacturing campus fills niche demand for crane-served and IOS-intensive logistics; significant signal of North Houston industrial market depth beyond standard distribution. Developers should track aerospace/defense and precision manufacturing tenancy in Houston's North corridor; the two-phase structure with Phase II flexibility suggests sponsor confidence in tenant demand pull, reducing speculative risk and signaling early-stage market tightening for specialized industrial in this submarket.

stories.title: Goodman Capital Leads $31M Condo Inventory Loan on Seattle-Area Resi Tower
stories.excerpt: Create World Real Estate has nabbed $30.6 million of condominium inventory financing for luxury residential tower east of Seattle, Commercial Observer has learned. Goodman Capital supplied a $25.625 million senior loan secured by the unsold residential units at Mari, a 20-story condo building in Downtown Bellevue, Wash., that opened in fall 2024. JEMM Capital Partners also provided a $4.95 million mezzanine loan as part of the transaction that supports the sponsor through the sale of the remaining condos in the 138-unit property. “Downtown Bellevue has become one of the Pacific Northwest’s most important urban centers, with major employers, shopping and transit close by, and Mari places residents in the middle of it,” Eric Goodman, managing partner at Goodman Capital, said in a statement. Located at 10232 Northeast 10th Street 10 miles east of Downtown Seattle, Mari was designed by MZA Architecture with interiors by B+H. Resident amenities include a sky lounge with a kitchen, a rooftop terrace with grilling stations, a fitness center and a yoga studio. Bellevue-based Create World Real Estate sealed a $95 million construction loan from Madison Realty Capital for the Mari condo tower in October 2021, Commercial Observer first reported at the time. “This transaction reflects our continued focus on financing high-quality assets in dynamic markets alongside experienced sponsors,” Matt Meltsner, partner and head of originations at JEMM Capital Partners, said in a statement. Create World Real Estate did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Goodman Capital leads $30.6M condo inventory loan, Mari tower, Bellevue, WA.
20-story, 138-unit luxury condo, opened fall 2024; 10 miles east Seattle.
Mezzanine layering and inventory financing signal below-expectations condo absorption; market stress emerging.
stories.summary: Goodman Capital and JEMM Capital Partners provided $30.6M in condo inventory financing ($25.6M senior + $4.95M mezzanine) for Mari, a 20-story, 138-unit luxury residential tower in Downtown Bellevue that opened in fall 2024. The property is located 10 miles east of Downtown Seattle near major employers and Brightline transit. The mezzanine layer indicates slower-than-projected unit absorption post-opening.
stories.impact: Mari's need for mezzanine layering and inventory financing less than 12 months after opening signals luxury condo absorption headwinds in Bellevue despite strong transit/employment fundamentals. Developers should flag inventory risk on condo projects in Pacific Northwest metros; rising interest rates and buyer credit/financing constraints may be suppressing unit absorption even in well-located, institutional-quality buildings, pressuring developer cash flow and project economics.

stories.title: Newmark Arranges Sale of 226-Unit Apartments in Chicago Suburbs
stories.excerpt: Newmark has facilitated the sale of Ashford at Geneva, a 226-unit multifamily community in Geneva, Illinois. Newmark Senior Managing Directors Susan Lawson, Liz Gagliardi and Chuck Johanns represented the seller, an investment entity controlled by Oak Residential Partners, in the sale to the buyer, an affiliate of Equus Capital Partners, Ltd. The property was approximately 97% occupied at the time of sale. “Ashford at Geneva is a well-maintained asset in an exceptional location, supported by strong surrounding demographics and home values,” said Lawson. “The property’s existing performance and opportunity for targeted improvements made it an attractive investment, with the potential to further enhance the resident experience and long-term value.” Following the acquisition, new ownership plans to implement a capital improvement program focused on apartment interiors, common areas and select exterior enhancements. Ashford at Geneva features one- and two-bedroom apartments averaging 962 square feet. Join us for the Connect Midwest Multifamily conference on the afternoon of Tuesday, June 8, 2027, at Joe’s Live in Rosemont, Illinois. The post Newmark Arranges Sale of 226-Unit Apartments in Chicago Suburbs appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Newmark arranges sale of Ashford at Geneva, Chicago suburbs, 226 units.
97% occupied; Equus Capital Partners acquires; 1-2BR avg 962 SF.
Stabilized, high-occupancy suburban Chicago asset trades; buyer plans value-add capex program.
stories.summary: Newmark facilitated the sale of Ashford at Geneva, a 226-unit multifamily community in Geneva, Illinois (Chicago suburbs), from Oak Residential Partners to an Equus Capital Partners affiliate. The property was 97% occupied at sale and features one- and two-bedroom units averaging 962 SF. New ownership plans targeted capital improvements to interiors, common areas, and exterior enhancements.
stories.impact: High-occupancy suburban Chicago asset sale to value-add buyer signals institutional capital interest in stabilized properties with modest upside via capex; limited relevance to development strategy unless it signals cap rate compression or demand for secondary bedroom/expanded SF units. Developers should monitor absorption and rent growth in suburban Chicago submarkets (Geneva, Fox Valley) to identify future infill/redevelopment opportunities.

stories.title: BWE Arranges $240M Recapitalization of Midwest Seniors Housing Portfolio
stories.excerpt: BWE arranged an approximately $240 million recapitalization of a multi-property seniors housing portfolio located across three major metropolitan markets in the Midwest. BWE served as exclusive capital markets advisor to O’Reilly Development Company, LLC, a Springfield, Missouri-based real estate developer and investor, in capitalizing the transaction. The portfolio comprises purpose-built Independent Living, Assisted Living, and Memory Care communities developed and managed by O’Reilly Development Company between 2019 and 2022. The assets are geographically diversified across three major Midwestern metropolitan statistical areas. The communities are fully stabilized, operating at occupancy levels ranging from 96% to 99%. The portfolio is managed by Arrow Senior Living, a St. Charles, Missouri-based regional operator. Arrow is co-invested alongside O’Reilly in the venture. “Our job was to make sure the capital markets outcome reflected the quality of this portfolio, and we’re proud of what the team delivered for O’Reilly and their residents,” said Ryan Stoll, National Director of Seniors Housing Capital Markets at BWE. Join us for the Connect Midwest Multifamily conference on the afternoon of Tuesday, June 8, 2027, at Joe’s Live in Rosemont, Illinois. The post BWE Arranges $240M Recapitalization of Midwest Seniors Housing Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: BWE arranges $240M recapitalization, O'Reilly Development seniors housing portfolio, Midwest.
Three metro portfolio: independent living, assisted living, memory care; 96-99% occupancy, 2019-2022 delivery.
Stabilized seniors housing commands institutional capital; Midwest demographics support aging-in-place demand.
stories.summary: BWE arranged a $240M recapitalization of a multi-property seniors housing portfolio owned by Springfield, Missouri-based O'Reilly Development Company across three major Midwest metropolitan areas. The portfolio comprises purpose-built Independent Living, Assisted Living, and Memory Care communities delivered between 2019 and 2022, operating at 96–99% occupancy and managed by Arrow Senior Living. Assets are fully stabilized with co-investment from both O'Reilly and Arrow.
stories.impact: Stabilized seniors housing in Midwest metros commanding institutional capital and strong occupancy reflects durable demographic demand (aging Baby Boomers, limited supply). Developers should monitor seniors housing delivery pipelines and occupancy trends across target Midwest markets; sustained high occupancy and recapitalization activity signal runway for new community development, especially in secondary/tertiary Midwest metros with favorable age demographics and limited modern supply.

stories.title: Extell Buys 1645 First Avenue on the Upper East Side for $28M
stories.excerpt: Gary Barnett’s Extell Development continues to stockpile small plots of land around Manhattan. Extell’s most recent acquisition made public since its previous buy on Monday is the $27.9 million purchase of 1645 First Avenue from Jay and Stuart Podolsky of Amsterdam Hospitality Group in the Yorkville section of Manhattan’s Upper East Side, according to property records. It’s unclear what Extell’s plans are for the plot of land where a good old-fashioned New York City dive bar once stood. The development firm declined to comment, but in 2021 it filed plans for a 542-unit housing project on the site, according to PincusCo. The midblock site sits on First Avenue between East 85th and East 86th streets. On Monday, it also surfaced that Extell had paid $18 million to Lighthouse Properties and Solil Management for 1190 Avenue of the Americas in Midtown, on the same block it’s building a 29-story office and retail building anchored by a full-sized Ikea store. Just weeks ago, Barnett closed on a $24 million deal for 87,000 square feet of air rights belonging to the Church of St. Mary the Virgin at 145 West 46th Street in Times Square, which is on the same block as the 1190 Avenue of the Americas property. Amsterdam Hospitality Group could not be reached for comment. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Extell buys 1645 First Avenue, Upper East Side Manhattan, $27.9M.
Small-plot land banking in Yorkville; 2021 filed plans for 542-unit residential.
Extell accumulating Manhattan assemblies; signals repositioning/development optionality, not immediate ground-up starts.
stories.summary: Extell Development purchased 1645 First Avenue in Manhattan's Yorkville section (Upper East Side) for $27.9M from Amsterdam Hospitality Group. The site, where a dive bar previously stood, sits on First Avenue between East 85th and East 86th streets. Extell filed plans in 2021 for a 542-unit housing project on the site; the firm declined to comment on current intentions. This is part of Extell's recent pattern of small-plot acquisitions around Manhattan.
stories.impact: Limited immediate development signal; Extell's land banking in Yorkville reflects optionality play rather than near-term starts. Developers should note Yorkville's emerging density interest but monitor rezoning trends, air-rights availability, and financing conditions in Upper East Side submarkets; small-plot assembly takes years and carries significant capital drag, typically signaling patient capital with long hold horizons, not rapid-turn development.

stories.title: RFR Seals $101M Refi on Downtown Miami Office Building
stories.excerpt: RFR has sealed a $101 million loan to refinance a repositioned Downtown Miami office building it acquired nearly five years ago, Commercial Observer can first report. Derby Lane Partners and Axonic Capital provided the loan for the developer’s 100 Biscayne property it purchased in January 2022 for $90 million. Since its acquisition, RFR has leased roughly 248,000 square feet to increase occupancy from under 60 percent to around 90 percent, according to the company. “When we acquired 100 Biscayne, our plan was to reposition the building into a true institutional-quality Class A boutique office building, broaden its tenant base and position it for long-term ownership,” Gaby Rosen, principal at RFR, said in a statement. “The leasing, rent and occupancy gains of the past four years, together with the long tenure of the building’s tenants, give us a stable foundation as long-term owners, and we remain confident in the Downtown Miami office market.” Rosen added that the property has a “continued value creation opportunity” through rent growth generated at the 317,000-square-foot property while also “capturing the upside of a significant portion of the building’s tenants in place below market leases.” Newmark arranged the transaction with a team consisting of Jordan Roeschlaub, Nick Scribani, Adam Spies and Josh King. Located at 100 Biscayne Boulevard across the street from Bayfront Park, the property stands out in the Miami market as the only Class A boutique waterfront office building in the city’s central business district, according to RFR. Tenants include French luxury goods conglomerate LVMH, Italian eyewear maker Luxottica, architecture firm Zyscovich, and engineering firm DeSimone. bullets: RFR refinances 100 Biscayne Boulevard, Downtown Miami office, $101M.
Repositioned from <60% to ~90% occupancy; 317K SF, 248K SF leased post-2022 acquisition.
Office refi/hold signals owner confidence; Miami downtown leasing momentum sustains institutional capital flow.
stories.summary: RFR sealed a $101M refinance on 100 Biscayne Boulevard in Downtown Miami, a 317K SF office building acquired in January 2022 for $90M. Since acquisition, RFR has leased approximately 248K SF, increasing occupancy from under 60% to around 90%. Derby Lane Partners and Axonic Capital provided the loan; RFR stated continued confidence in Downtown Miami office market and value creation through rent growth.
stories.impact: RFR's successful repositioning and refinance of Downtown Miami office signals sustained institutional capital interest and leasing momentum in an office-challenged market. Developers should monitor Downtown Miami office absorption, rent growth, and tenant quality trends; if repositioning and 90% occupancy can support refinance at modest expansion over acquisition price, it suggests limited structural arbitrage for new office development, and capital should focus on mixed-use/residential adjacencies and adaptive reuse rather than speculative office starts.

stories.title: Peak Capital Sells Upper East Side Mixed-Use Building for $23M
stories.excerpt: David Gomez and Alex Rabin of Peak Capital Real Estate have sold an Upper East Side mixed-use building. The firm offloaded 308 East 78th Street to an unlikely buyer in Japanese staircase fabricator Yokomori Manufacturing Company, which paid $22.8 million for the six-story residential building with a restaurant on the ground floor, according to property records. The restaurant space is currently leased to Heidi’s House by the Side of the Road and its affiliated adjacent bar Ed’s Elbow Room. Peak did not immediately respond to a request for comment while Yokomori, which does not appear to have any operations stateside apart from an industrial site in Louisville, Ky., could not be reached for comment. The deal closed in late October but appeared in property records late Tuesday afternoon. But Peak will walk away with a profit after buying the property only in January 2025 for $14.8 million from Abram Orwasher’s Arsalou Realty, according to the last deed transfer on file. The sale to Yokomori comes as investors seem to be taking an increased interest in the Upper East Side. Roger Equities acquired a movie theater site at 1001 Third Avenue for $41 million with $37 million in financing for redevelopment, Commercial Observer reported on Tuesday. In late October, a joint venture between Grand Cru Real Estate and Visabe secured $52.5 million of construction financing for a 28-unit condominium project at 1527 York Avenue. Both of the recent financings came from S3 Capital. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Peak Capital sells 308 East 78th Street, Upper East Side, $22.8M to Yokomori Manufacturing.
Six-story mixed-use: residential + ground-floor restaurant; Peak bought Jan 2025 for $14.8M.
Opportunistic flip to non-traditional buyer; minimal developer signal on residential fundamentals.
stories.summary: Peak Capital Real Estate sold 308 East 78th Street on the Upper East Side to Japanese staircase fabricator Yokomori Manufacturing Company for $22.8M. The six-story mixed-use building comprises residential units and a ground-floor restaurant (Heidi's House by the Side of the Road and Ed's Elbow Room). Peak acquired the property in January 2025 for $14.8M, realizing a ~$8M profit in less than one year. The buyer's primary operations are industrial (staircase fabrication in Louisville, KY).
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development strategy. Peak's rapid flip and sale to an industrial buyer outside traditional real estate markets suggests the seller captured opportunistic property market inefficiency rather than fundamental residential demand signal. Yokomori's acquisition rationale is unclear; developers should disregard this transaction as a bellwether for Upper East Side residential demand or values.
